steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Electromagnet: A coil of wire (solenoid) with a current flowing through it, which produces a magnetic field. Unlike a permanent magnet, an electromagnet can be switched on and off by turning the current on and off. | Solenoid: A coil of wire that produces a strong, uniform magnetic field inside it when a current flows. The field inside is strong and parallel to the axis; the field outside is similar to a bar magnet. | Motor effect: When a current-carrying wire is placed in a magnetic field, the wire experiences a force. This is the motor effect. The force is greatest when the wire is perpendicular to the magnetic field. | Fleming's left-hand rule: A rule to determine the direction of the force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field.
